potato-baked-peel-not-eaten-with-cheese.title: Baked Potato, Peel Not Eaten, with Cheese

content.title: About
content.content: Baked potato with the peel removed, served with melted cheese. The dish combines the soft interior of the potato with a flavorful, slightly browned cheese, creating a nutritious and satisfying snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Baking retains most of the B‑vitamins and potassium found in potatoes.
Cheese adds calcium and protein to the baked potato.
Removing the peel helps eliminate possible pesticide residues and improves texture.
In Russia, baked potatoes are traditionally served with cottage cheese or sour cream; the cheese version became popular in Western cuisines.

items.title: Potassium source
items.content: Potatoes are rich in potassium, which supports normal heart and muscle function.

items.title: Vitamin C content
items.content: Heat processing preserves some vitamin C, which helps strengthen the immune system.

items.title: Fiber content
items.content: Even without the skin, the flesh provides dietary fiber beneficial for digestion.

items.title: Protein and calcium from cheese
items.content: Cheese contributes complete protein and calcium, important for bones and muscles.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: The dish offers a quick source of energy thanks to the carbohydrates in the potato.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Cheese increases the calorie density, so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: People with lactose intolerance should choose lactose‑free cheese or omit it.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Cheese can be salty; those monitoring sodium intake should select low‑salt varieties.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cut the baked potato in half, sprinkle grated cheese, and return to the oven until the cheese forms a golden crust. Serve hot, optionally topped with herbs, sour cream, or yogurt.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the prepared dish in the refrigerator for up to 2 days in an airtight container. Reheat in the oven or microwave to retain the cheese's crisp crust.
